method: OPEN AND QUOTED, from the RCH Melbourne Clinical Practice Guideline 'Quetiapine Poisoning' (Last Updated April 2019), retrieved 2026-09-23. Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. LICENCE: Free to read but NOT openly licensed -- each page carries '(c) 2026 The Royal Children's Hospital'. Quoted with attribution on the same footing as the 14 RCH guidelines and the Immunisation Handbook guidelines already in this compendium.

claims.claim: **Assess:** every deliberate self-poisoning or significant accidental ingestion · any symptomatic child · **any child whose developmental age doesn't fit accidental poisoning — consider non-accidental poisoning.**
claims.source_text: All children with deliberate self-poisoning or significant (see below) accidental ingestion. Any symptomatic child … Any child in whom the developmental age is inconsistent with accidental poisoning, as non-accidental poisoning should be considered.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Quetiapine Poisoning' (Last Updated April 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Quetiapine_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Significant dose:** 10 mg/kg in an adult; **more than 3 g — or more than 100 mg in a child under 12 — may cause severe toxicity.**
claims.source_text: 10 mg/kg is significant in an adult whilst >3 g (Greater than 100 mg in a child <12 years) may be associated with severe toxicity.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Quetiapine Poisoning' (Last Updated April 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Quetiapine_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Adolescents: under 3 g usually means mild CNS depression and tachycardia; over 3 g can cause delirium, coma, hypotension and, rarely, seizures (under 5%).**
claims.source_text: In adolescents who have ingested less than 3 grams expect mild CNS depression and tachycardia. Ingestions greater than 3 grams can cause delirium, coma, hypotension and (rarely) seizures (<5%).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Quetiapine Poisoning' (Last Updated April 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Quetiapine_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Tablets are 25–400 mg, immediate or modified release:** identify the exact product and tablet size, and calculate the maximum possible dose per kg.
claims.source_text: Presented as immediate or modified-release tablets in 25–400 mg - if possible determine the exact name and tablet size Calculate the maximum possible dose per kg
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Quetiapine Poisoning' (Last Updated April 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Quetiapine_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Immediate release peaks at 1–2 hours; modified-release overdose brings delayed onset and prolonged symptoms**, for example 24–72 hours.
claims.source_text: The immediate-release formulation has rapid oral absorption with peak 1-2 hours post ingestion. … In modified release overdose, expect delayed onset and prolonged duration of symptoms, eg for 24-72 hours.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Quetiapine Poisoning' (Last Updated April 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Quetiapine_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Recreational drugs are common co-ingestants.** ⚠️ **Every intentional adolescent self-poisoning needs a paracetamol screen and admission.**
claims.source_text: Recreational drugs are common co-ingestants … All intentional self-poisonings in adolescents require screening for paracetamol ingestion and admission
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Quetiapine Poisoning' (Last Updated April 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Quetiapine_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Look for CNS depression (any decrease is significant), tachycardia and hypotension.**
claims.source_text: CNS depression – any decrease is significant Tachycardia Hypotension
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Quetiapine Poisoning' (Last Updated April 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Quetiapine_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **ECG at presentation and repeat at 4 hours until normal.** A long QTc is usually insignificant: no torsades de pointes has been reported and it does not correlate with toxicity. **Paracetamol level in all intentional overdoses.**
claims.source_text: ECG: (initially and repeat at 4 hours till normal). Long QTc, however is usually insignificant as there are no reports of torsades de pointes and it does not correlate with toxicity. … Paracetamol level in all intentional overdoses.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Quetiapine Poisoning' (Last Updated April 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Quetiapine_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Hypotension: 20 mL/kg normal saline bolus, repeated if still hypotensive; then a noradrenaline infusion. Adrenaline paradoxically worsens hypotension.**
claims.source_text: Hypotension: treat with bolus 20 mL/kg N Saline. Repeat if remains hypotensive. Ongoing hypotension – treat with noradrenaline infusion as adrenaline paradoxically worsens hypotension
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Quetiapine Poisoning' (Last Updated April 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Quetiapine_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Charcoal only for a massive ingestion within 1 hour, or once intubated.** Enhanced elimination is ineffective and **there is no antidote.**
claims.source_text: Consider charcoal if massive ingestion and within 1 hour, or if required intubation (after airway protection). … Enhance elimination – ineffective Antidote - Nil
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Quetiapine Poisoning' (Last Updated April 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Quetiapine_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Watch for urinary retention** — consider it as a cause of agitation — and place an IDC if needed.
claims.source_text: Watch for urinary retention and manage with an IDC if required (consider as a cause of agitation).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Quetiapine Poisoning' (Last Updated April 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Quetiapine_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Monitor 4 hours** for ingestions under 10 mg/kg and under 100 mg; **monitor 12 hours** for over 100 mg, over 10 mg/kg, or any sustained-release product.
claims.source_text: Ingestion <10 mg/kg and <100 mg – monitor for 4 hours Ingestion >100 mg or >10 mg/kg or sustained release - monitor for 12 hours
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Quetiapine Poisoning' (Last Updated April 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Quetiapine_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Transfer any child who needs noradrenaline or intubation.**
claims.source_text: Consider transfer when Children requiring treatment with noradrenaline or intubation.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Quetiapine Poisoning' (Last Updated April 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Quetiapine_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge when GCS and ECG are normal and the observation period is complete.**
claims.source_text: Consider discharge when Normal GCS Normal ECG Period of observation as above
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Quetiapine Poisoning' (Last Updated April 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Quetiapine_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Before discharging an adolescent after a deliberate ingestion**, assess self-harm risk and other drug and alcohol use.
claims.source_text: Prior to discharge, adolescents who present with deliberate ingestions need a risk assessment regarding the likelihood of further ingestions or other attempts to self-harm. … Assessment of other drug and alcohol use should also be undertaken.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Quetiapine Poisoning' (Last Updated April 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Quetiapine_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23
